title: 航空工学概論
subtitle: Introduction to Aircraft Design
educationalGoal: Students will: (1) learn all the engineering (aerospace, structure, equipment, control) needed to conduct research, development, design and manufacture of aircraft (2) learn the relationships among the fields of professional engineering (3) learn about aircraft design and manufacturing processes (4) consider regional issues that can be solved by aeronautics
advice: This is a basic introduction to aircraft design course. We will cover the following materials: 1. Atmosphere 2. Types of aircraft, such as fixed wing and rotorcraft 3. Lift and drag 4. Jet engines 5. Stability and Control 6. Structure, materials and structural design 7. Aircraft design process Students are expected to understand the meaning of terms and formulas. Students are expected to solve the exercises on their own. Students should be aware of the teacher's instructions in the class, because the schedule of quizzes, tests and reports may change as the class progresses. Students should not be absent from the class, as they may miss handouts.
books: Introduction to Aeronautics, Second edition (in Japanese), Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: Completed the courses in Industrial Mechanics and Mechanical Mechanics. Basic knowledge of mechanics (kinematics and moment of force).

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the role of aircraft components.
Be able to understand the basic content of the aeronautics (aerodynamics, structure, equipment, control).
Be able to describe performance using numerical values such as aircraft weight and center of gravity.
Be able to understand and explain aircraft development, design and manufacturing processes.

achievementLevels.ideal: (1) Understand the basics of the major fields of aircraft design (aerodynamics, structure, equipment, control) required to perform research, development, design and manufacture of aircraft. (2) Understand the relationship between the major fields of aircraft design. (3) Discuss the performance of aircraft using numerical values such as weight and center of gravity.

lessons.content: Chapter 3: Aircraft and Spacecraft types Chapter 4: Lift and drag, Two-dimensional wings

Chapter 8: Guidance and navigation Chapter 9: Structure and materials
